lines.text: You liked The Matrix. How would a computer find other films that feel like it, without just matching titles?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. SimilityVectorEmbedding is a set of Jupyter notebooks from AlgoÉTS that turn a movie catalog into embeddings, which are lists of numbers capturing meaning, and then search them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One text per film: title, year, genres, actors, director and summary. A sentence-transformer model encodes it into a vector, and the vectors are stored in PostgreSQL with pgvector. The saved run loads 631 films.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You type a title, it's matched even if you're a little off, and the rest of the catalog is ranked by cosine similarity. There's also a Gradio page where you can try one title, several, or rated ones.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, that's the fun part. Each folder pairs a notebook with another approach: Qdrant for vectors, BM25 for keywords, Neo4j for a graph of genres and people, and even a local language model through Ollama.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So you can compare how each one sees the same catalog.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. The article and the written page have the details.
